themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions in Midwood/Ocean Parkway have spiked 286% this week with 54 complaints versus a baseline of 14 per week, suggesting a sudden deterioration in road surface quality or widespread pothole formation requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 54 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs 14.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (286% increase)
Z-score of 8.63 indicates statistically extreme deviation from baseline
284 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (215 alterations) suggests possible street infrastructure disruption from construction
reporting_angles: Door-knock survey of residents on major avenues (Ocean Parkway, Coney Island Ave, Flatbush Ave) to document specific street hazards and pothole locations
FOIL request to DOT for recent street repair schedules and budgets in CD 314 to determine if city is responding to complaints

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Activity Surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matters jumped 248% this week with 10 complaints versus a 2.9 weekly average, indicating a sudden spike in incidents requiring police response but not serious enough for 911.
evidence: 10 non-emergency police complaints THIS WEEK vs 2.9 weekly average (248% spike)
Z-score of 5.23 indicates highly anomalous week
Concurrent spike in street/sidewalk noise (55 complaints 2 weeks ago, 307% above baseline) and encampments (4 complaints 2 weeks ago, 967% above baseline) suggests overlapping public disorder issues
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD 61st Precinct to understand what types of non-emergency incidents drove this week's surge—quality-of-life enforcement, disorderly conduct, trespassing, etc.
Interview residents on high-complaint blocks about whether they feel less safe this week

themes_detail.label: Sewer and Sanitation Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints spiked 300% two weeks ago (19 complaints vs 4.8 baseline) and remain elevated, with concurrent 500% spike in unsanitary pigeon complaints last week, suggesting a potential environmental health hazard tied to sewer overflow or blockage.
evidence: 19 sewer complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs 4.8 weekly average (300% spike, z-score 7.69)
3 unsanitary pigeon condition complaints LAST WEEK vs 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score 5.0)
933 unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days (third-largest category after heat/hot water and illegal parking) suggests baseline sanitation stress in district
reporting_angles: FOIL DEP for sewer backup and overflow reports in CD 314 over past 30 days; map incidents to specific blocks
Investigative piece on whether aging sewer infrastructure in Midwood is at capacity; interview DEP about planned upgrades

themes_detail.label: Illegal Wildlife and Encampment Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Illegal animal complaints surged 1100% two weeks ago (3 vs 0.2 baseline) and encampment reports jumped 967% (4 vs 0.4 baseline), signaling either a genuinely new phenomenon or a shift in community awareness of visible disorder on streets.
evidence: 3 illegal animal complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs 0.2 weekly average (1100% increase, z-score 6.35)
4 encampment complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs 0.4 weekly average (967% increase, z-score 5.21)
Both spikes occurred in same week, suggesting coordinated issue or reporting campaign rather than separate phenomena
reporting_angles: Canvass blocks with highest complaint density to document types of animals being kept illegally and visible encampments; photograph locations
Interview NYC Parks Enforcement and Animal Care & Control about recent enforcement activity in Midwood—whether complaints reflect new issues or new enforcement

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Damage Wave
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints exploded 900% two weeks ago with 5 complaints versus a baseline of 0.5 per week, potentially indicating systematic vandalism or a single incident affecting multiple signs.
evidence: 5 street sign damage complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs 0.5 weekly average (900% spike, z-score 6.36)
Highly localized incident suggests potential vandalism cluster rather than citywide infrastructure failure
May be early warning of broader public space degradation occurring alongside other sanitation/disorder spikes
reporting_angles: FOIL DOT for list of specific damaged signs reported 2 weeks ago and their locations; visit sites to assess whether damage is uniform (suggesting coordinated vandalism) or random
Brief item documenting the spike and asking residents if they noticed vandalism activity around that date
